question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{21}(xy)^{2}, & 0\le x\le 3,\,1\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X>1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{21}(xy)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{21}{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{21}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{63}({2}^{3}-{1}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>1) & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[{3}^{3}-{1}^{3}] \\  & =\frac{26}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$
